description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a beloved Indian classic known for its rich, creamy tomato-based gravy and tender pieces of chicken. This recipe captures the authentic flavors, balancing tanginess with a subtle sweetness and aromatic spices. It is truly a feast for the senses, perfect for a comforting family meal or a special occasion.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the cubed chicken with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook until lightly browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tbsp butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, green cardamom, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Saute for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Base
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add the soaked cashews (drained). Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to cook down.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods (if you can find them easily). Carefully transfer the tomato-cashew mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. For a silkier gravy, pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve back into the clean pan, pressing down on solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the cooked chicken, sugar, and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the gravy flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and cook for 1-2 minutes more, ensuring not to boil after adding cream. Taste and adjust salt or sugar if needed.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired. Serve the Classic Butter Chicken hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice for a truly authentic Indian meal.

tips: For extra smoky flavor, grill or pan-fry the marinated chicken until slightly charred before adding it to the gravy.
Soaking cashews is crucial for a smooth and creamy gravy. If you dont have cashews, almonds can be used as a substitute.
Always add cream at the very end and avoid boiling the gravy after its added, to prevent it from curdling and to maintain its rich texture.
article:
Mastering the Art of Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian delicacy, renowned for its rich, creamy texture and subtly spiced tomato gravy, has transcended borders to become a global favorite. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook looking to explore the vibrant world of Indian cuisine, understanding the nuances of authentic Murgh Makhani will elevate your culinary skills and delight your taste buds. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create a restaurant-quality Butter Chicken right in your own kitchen.

## What is Classic Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Classic Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, literally translates to "chicken with butter." Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s, it was a creation of the Moti Mahal restaurant. The dish was born out of a desire to utilize leftover tandoori chicken by simmering it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was a revelation: tender pieces of chicken bathed in a velvety, slightly sweet, and tangy sauce, balanced with aromatic spices.

What sets Murgh Makhani apart is its intricate balance of flavors. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and spices before being grilled or pan-fried, imparting a smoky depth. The gravy, the true soul of the dish, is a luscious blend of pureed tomatoes, cashews (for thickness), ginger, garlic, and a medley of spices like garam masala, cumin, and fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). A generous swirl of butter and cream at the end provides its signature richness, making Butter Chicken an undeniably comforting and luxurious meal.

## Ingredients for Authentic Butter Chicken

Crafting authentic Murgh Makhani requires fresh, quality ingredients for both the chicken marinade and the rich gravy. Don't skimp on these; they are the foundation of the dish's incredible flavor.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 tsp red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp lemon juice
*   Salt to taste

For the Gravy:
*   2 tbsp unsalted butter
*   1 tbsp oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste
*   1 cup tomato puree (from fresh ripe tomatoes or canned diced tomatoes)
*   1/2 cup cashews, soaked in hot water for 15 minutes
*   1/2 tsp red chili powder
*   1 tsp cumin powder
*   1 tsp coriander powder
*   1/2 tsp turmeric powder
*   1/2 tsp garam masala
*   1 tbsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tbsp sugar (optional, to balance acidity)
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

Garnish: Fresh coriander leaves, a swirl of cream.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Murgh Makhani

Follow these steps carefully to achieve a truly memorable Butter Chicken.

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor absorption.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a grill pan, heavy-bottomed skillet, or oven to a high temperature. Add a little oil and cook the marinated chicken pieces until they are nicely charred and cooked through. If using an oven, bake at 200°C (400°F) for 15-20 minutes. Set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Gravy Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter and oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Build the Gravy:** Stir in the tomato puree. Add the soaked and pureed cashews (blend cashews with a little water until smooth). Now, add the dry spices: red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook the mixture, stirring frequently, until the oil separates from the masala, indicating the spices are well cooked. This may take 10-15 minutes.

5.  **Simmer and Smooth:** Add about 1/2 to 1 cup of water or chicken broth to the gravy base. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. For a truly silky smooth gravy, allow it to cool slightly, then blend it with an immersion blender or carefully transfer to a regular blender and process until completely smooth. Strain the gravy back into the pot for an even finer texture (optional but recommended).

6.  **Combine and Finish:** Return the smooth gravy to the heat. Stir in the cooked chicken pieces. Add the crushed kasoori methi and sugar (if using). Bring to a gentle simmer. Finally, stir in the heavy cream and a final knob of butter. Cook for another 5 minutes, allowing the cream to warm through but not boil vigorously. Taste and adjust salt or sugar as needed.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving that perfect restaurant-style Butter Chicken isn't just about following steps; it's about technique and attention to detail.

*   **Marination Time is Key:** The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken:** Don't skip browning the chicken. The smoky, slightly charred edges contribute significantly to the authentic flavor profile of Murgh Makhani.
*   **Cook the Masala Well:** Ensure the onion-tomato-spice base is cooked until the oil separates. This "bhuno" process deepens the flavors and prevents a raw spice taste.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blending the gravy until absolutely smooth is crucial for that luxurious, velvety texture. Straining it further enhances this.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is non-negotiable for authentic Murgh Makhani. Crush it between your palms before adding to release its aroma.
*   **Balance Flavors:** The beauty of Butter Chicken lies in its balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Adjust sugar and salt at the end. A pinch of black pepper can also enhance the flavor.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of Indian breads and rice.

*   **Naan Bread:** Garlic naan or plain naan is the quintessential accompaniment, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lighter contrast and allows the flavors of the Murgh Makhani to shine.
*   **Raita:** A cooling cucumber raita or plain yogurt helps to cut through the richness of the dish.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple onion and tomato salad with a squeeze of lemon adds freshness.

## Variations and FAQs

**Can I make it vegetarian?**
Absolutely! Substitute chicken with paneer (Indian cheese), tofu, or mixed vegetables (potatoes, peas, carrots) and follow the same gravy recipe.

**How can I make it spicier?**
Increase the amount of red chili powder or add a finely chopped green chili to the gravy base.

**Can I prepare the gravy ahead of time?**
Yes, the gravy can be made a day or two in advance and stored in the refrigerator. Reheat gently and add the cooked chicken and cream just before serving.

**Is it possible to make it healthier?**
You can reduce the amount of butter and cream, opting for low-fat cream or a touch of coconut milk for richness. Increase the cashew quantity for a thicker, naturally creamy texture.

**What if I don't have kasoori methi?**
While highly recommended, if you absolutely cannot find it, you can omit it. However, the unique aroma and slight bitterness it imparts are key to authentic Butter Chicken.

Making classic Butter Chicken is a culinary journey that promises incredibly satisfying results. With this guide, you now have all the tools and knowledge to create a truly delicious Murgh Makhani that will impress family and friends alike. Enjoy the process, savor the aromas, and relish every spoonful of this beloved Indian masterpiece!
